summary: CLIFT trains an open web agent (Gemma 4 31B + LoRA) with GRPO using per-step rewards from natural-language self-verification questions that are kept only if a conformal-style lift certifier shows they agree with a frontier training-time judge (Claude Opus 4.6). At test time the certified question bank selects among K rollouts without an external judge. It reports state-of-the-art open-source results on WebArena Infinity, transfer to GPT-5.5 on VisualWebArena, and zero-shot gains on Online Mind2Web.

claims.claim: CLIFT+CTS achieves state of the art among open-source web agents on WebArena Infinity.
claims.evidence: Table 3: Gemma-4 + CLIFT + CTS (K=3) 74.6 vs base 61.8 and Gemini 3 Flash + BU 70.1 over 9 apps. Compares a best-of-3 selected policy against published single-rollout leaderboard entries; the two apps where Gemini leads are dismissed as 'integer-rounding noise'. No variance.

claims.claim: Certified step rewards beat vanilla GRPO with the same judge.
claims.evidence: Table 6: vanilla GRPO 64.7 (+2.9), CLIFT 72.6 (+10.8), CTS adds +2.0; CTS improves/ties/regresses 5/4/0 apps. Single training run, no seeds.

claims.claim: Bank trained with the open model transfers to GPT-5.5 on VWA and reaches SOTA.
claims.evidence: Table 4: GPT-5.5 + CLIFT+CTS (K=4) 53.7 vs WALT 52.9 (WALT is prior work by overlapping Salesforce authors) and SGV 50.2; 0.8-point margin with K=4 rollouts vs single-rollout baselines, no variance.

claims.claim: Translated, recalibrated bank improves live-web agents zero-shot on OM2W.
claims.evidence: §4.3/Fig. 5: GPT-5.5 high 49.7 -> 61.0 at K=4; Gemma-4 40.0 -> 45.0. OM2W is scored by an LLM rubric judge; bank recalibrated on OM2W rollouts (App. A.4) with unclear disjointness from the 300 evaluation tasks.

patterns.note: Distills a frontier LLM judge into a calibrated self-verification bank; the judge itself is not validated against humans.
GRPO with certified dense rewards beats vanilla GRPO by ~8 points on WAI (single run).
Uses expensive judge only at training time and cheap self-verification at inference.

methodology.sample: WAI 9-app slice (1,140 tasks across apps per Table 3), VWA three environments, OM2W 300 live tasks; training on 1,886 WAI + 1,272 VWA synthesized tasks.
methodology.baselines: Published leaderboard numbers (Gemini 3 Flash + BU, Qwen 3.5+, Kimi K2.5, SGV, WALT) run at single rollout; in-house base and vanilla GRPO.
methodology.models: Gemma 4 31B (trained), GPT-5.5 (inference), Claude Opus 4.6 as training judge; Claude Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.5 for task synthesis.
methodology.ablations: Table 6 component decomposition on WAI only.
methodology.contamination_controls: App. A.2 states training pipeline never read evaluation tasks; OM2W recalibration uses OM2W rollouts, split not clearly specified.

standards.artifacts: No code or bank release link found; prompts in App. A.1.

biases.detail: Best-of-K selected trajectories compared against single-rollout leaderboard baselines for SOTA claims.
Single run, margins of 0.8 (VWA) and 4.5 (WAI) points without CIs.
OM2W scored by LLM rubric; training judge Opus 4.6 not validated against humans; authors acknowledge judge bias risk (§5).
Baseline rows taken from public boards/papers rather than rerun.
OM2W bank recalibrated on OM2W rollouts; disjointness from evaluation tasks not stated.
No code or certified bank released.

coi.affiliations: All six authors Salesforce AI Research.
coi.vendor_products_evaluated: Compares against and narrowly beats WALT (Prabhu et al. 2025), prior Salesforce work co-authored by Prabhu, Dai, Chen, Xu; does not evaluate a commercial Salesforce product.
coi.detail: Vendor-affiliated, SOTA claim partly over own prior baseline; no commercial product evaluated.

verdict_reason: off-topic: RL training and test-time selection for browser web agents, not software engineering harnesses; additionally SOTA claims rest on compute-mismatched comparisons, single runs, and an unvalidated LLM judge.
applicability: Does not transfer to a reference team: the team will not RL-train web agents, and the method depends on URL-state traces and a frontier judge. The only portable idea is turning expensive LLM-judge feedback into a small calibrated checklist of verification questions reused across agent hosts; the paper's own discussion points to replacing such questions with executable assertions, which for a Java the pipeline means tests and schema checks rather than this method.

conflicts_with.detail: That paper finds agent self-authored verification unreliable without exogenous checks; CLIFT relies on self-verification at test time, mitigated only by calibration against a training-time LLM judge.
